source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How is the inner cannula reinserted after cleaning?
questions.rationale: The inner cannula is inserted in the direction of its curvature and locked to the outer cannula flange.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tracheostomy Care (PDF p. 40)
questions.quote: Insert the inner cannula in the direction of its curvature

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which dressing is used under a tracheostomy flange?
questions.rationale: Use a commercial non-raveling dressing or a folded 4x4; never cut gauze or use cotton-filled squares (fibers can be aspirated).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tracheostomy Care (PDF p. 40)
questions.quote: Avoid using cotton-filled gauze square or cutting the 4in x 4in gauze

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which suction catheter size is used for an adult?
questions.rationale: Adults Fr 12–18; children Fr 8–10; infants Fr 5–8.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Suctioning (PDF p. 40)
questions.quote: Adults: Fr 12-18

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which catheter is used for oropharyngeal suctioning?
questions.rationale: A Yankauer catheter is used for oropharyngeal suctioning.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Suctioning (PDF p. 40)
questions.quote: Yankauer suction catheter is used for oropharyngeal

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How long should one suction pass last?
questions.rationale: Apply suction 5–10 seconds; the whole attempt lasts 10–15 seconds, and total suctioning is limited to 5 minutes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Suctioning (PDF p. 41)
questions.quote: The whole suction attempt should last only 10-15 secs

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When is suction applied during catheter insertion?
questions.rationale: No suction during insertion; apply intermittent suction while rotating and withdrawing.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Suctioning (PDF p. 41)
questions.quote: Do not apply suction during insertion

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How is an unconscious client positioned for oral suctioning?
questions.rationale: Unconscious clients are placed lateral facing the nurse to drain secretions; conscious clients semi-Fowler's.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Suctioning (PDF p. 41)
questions.quote: Position unconscious client in lateral position facing you

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How far is the catheter inserted for nasopharyngeal suction in an adult?
questions.rationale: Measure from nose tip to earlobe, about 13 cm (5 in) in adults.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nasopharyngeal Suctioning (PDF p. 41)
questions.quote: Measure the distance between the tip of the nose and earlobe or about 13cm. (5in.) for an adult

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How long should the nurse wait between tracheal suction passes?
questions.rationale: Allow 2–3 minutes with oxygen between suctions when possible.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tracheal Suctioning (PDF p. 42)
questions.quote: Allow 2-3 mins with 02. as appropriate between suctions when possible

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which tube is used to control bleeding esophageal varices?
questions.rationale: The triple-lumen Sengstaken-Blakemore tube treats bleeding varices; Miller-Abbott decompresses the intestine.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Enteral Tubes (PDF p. 42)
questions.quote: Sengstaken-Blakemore tube – triple-lumen tube used to treat bleeding esophageal varices

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How is NG tube length measured?
questions.rationale: Measure from the tip of the nose to the earlobe to the xiphoid process.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Inserting an NG Tube (PDF p. 43)
questions.quote: tip of the client’s nose to tip of the earlobe up to the xyphoid process.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why is a water-soluble lubricant used for NG insertion?
questions.rationale: Water-soluble lubricant dissolves if it enters the lungs; oil-based lubricant can cause lipid pneumonia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Inserting an NG Tube (PDF p. 43)
questions.quote: A water-soluble lubricant dissolves if the tube accidentally, enters the lungs.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Once the NG tube reaches the oropharynx, how should the client position the head?
questions.rationale: Tilting the head forward helps the tube pass into the esophagus rather than the trachea.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Inserting an NG Tube (PDF p. 43)
questions.quote: Tilting the head forward facilitates passage of the tube into the posterior pharynx and esophagus

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which aspirate pH suggests gastric placement of a feeding tube?
questions.rationale: Gastric contents are usually pH 1 to 5.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tube Feeding (PDF p. 44)
questions.quote: Gastric contents are commonly pH1 to 5

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After a gastrostomy feeding, how long should the client stay upright?
questions.rationale: The client remains sitting or slightly elevated right lateral for 30 minutes to reduce aspiration.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gastrostomy (PDF p. 44)
questions.quote: ask the client to remain in the sitting position or slightly elevated right lateral position for 30 minutes

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How often are enteral feeding bag and tubing replaced?
questions.rationale: The bag and tubing are replaced every 24 hours.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Enteral Feeding (PDF p. 43)
questions.quote: The bag and tubing should be replaced every 24 hours

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should TPN be discontinued?
questions.rationale: TPN is tapered slowly to prevent hyperinsulinemia and rebound hypoglycemia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Parenteral Nutrition (PDF p. 44)
questions.quote: the TPN infusion rates are decreased slowly to prevent hyperinsulinemia and rebound hypoglycemia

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which stool finding suggests upper GI bleeding?
questions.rationale: Black, tarry stool suggests upper GI bleeding; normal adult stool is brown and formed.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Characteristics of Feces (PDF p. 44)
questions.quote: Tarry

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How high is a HIGH cleansing enema container held?
questions.rationale: High enema: 12–18 inches with position changes; low enema: no higher than 12 inches.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Enema (PDF p. 45)
questions.quote: Container is held 12-18 inches above the rectum

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which enema is given mainly to expel flatus?
questions.rationale: Carminative enemas (60–80 mL in adults) expel flatus; return-flow enemas also do.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Enema (PDF p. 45)
questions.quote: Given primarily to expel flatus

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How far is a rectal tube inserted in an adult for an enema?
questions.rationale: Adults: Fr 22–32 inserted 3–4 inches; children 2–3 inches; infants 1–1.5 inches.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Rectal Tube (PDF p. 46)
questions.quote: Adult — Fr. 22-32 inserted 3-4 inches in the anal canal

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which ostomy has liquid output with enzymes that damage skin and cannot be regulated?
questions.rationale: Ileostomy drainage is liquid, unregulated, enzyme-rich, and needs continuous appliance wear.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bowel Ostomies (PDF p. 46)
questions.quote: Ileostomy

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Colostomy irrigation is appropriate for which ostomy?
questions.rationale: Irrigation is used only for sigmoid or descending colostomies, which produce formed stool and can be regulated.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Colostomy Irrigation (PDF p. 47)
questions.quote: used only for client who have a sigmoid or descending colostomy

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A new stoma looks dusky purple. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: A healthy stoma is red and moist; pale or dusky bluish-purple indicates impaired circulation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stoma Assessment (PDF p. 48)
questions.quote: Very pale or darker-colored stomas with a dusky bluish or purplish hue indicate impaired blood circulation

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which advice helps a client with flatulence?
questions.rationale: Limit carbonated drinks, straws, and gum (swallowed air) and gas-forming foods.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Promoting Defecation (PDF p. 47)
questions.quote: Limit carbonated beverages. the use of drinking straws and chewing gum

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: During an enema the client reports cramps. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Lower the container or clamp the tube for 30 seconds, then restart slowly.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Administering Enema (PDF p. 46)
questions.quote: lower the container or clamp the tube to stop the flow for 30 sec. then restart the flow at a slow rate
